openwrt_wiki.einleitung: The Aruba AP-303H is a Qualcomm based dual-radio 802.11ac Wave 2 2x2:2 hospitality and branch AP with internal antennas, three Gigabit Ethernet ports, PoE out and USB host interface. Supports wall-box and desk mount deployments. The Aruba Instant On AP11D is a cheaper version of this device based on the same platform and the OpenWrt firmware for AP-303H can also be flashed onto the AP11D.
openwrt_wiki.installation: -> [[docs:guide-user:installation:generic.flashing|Install OpenWrt (generic explanation)]] - Get the OpenWrt initramfs image. Rename it to ''ipq40xx.ari'' and put it into the TFTP server root directory. - Configure the TFTP server to be reachable at 192.168.1.75/24. - Connect the machine running the TFTP server to the **E0** (!) ethernet port of the access point, as it only tries to pull from the WAN port. - Connect to the serial console. Interrupt autobooting by pressing Enter when prompted. (For information on the serial pinout see [[:toh:aruba:ap-303#serial|Aruba AP 303 serial]]) - Configure the bootargs and bootcmd for OpenWrt\\ $ setenv bootargs_openwrt "setenv bootargs console=ttyMSM0,9600n8" $ setenv nandboot_openwrt "run bootargs_openwrt; ubi part aos1; ubi read 0x85000000 kernel; set fdt_high 0x87000000; bootm 0x85000000" $ setenv ramboot_openwrt "run bootargs_openwrt; setenv ipaddr 192.168.1.105; setenv serverip 192.168.1.75; netget; set fdt_high 0x87000000; bootm" $ setenv bootcmd "run nandboot_openwrt" $ saveenv - Load OpenWrt into RAM:$ run ramboot_openwrt - After OpenWrt booted, transfer the OpenWrt sysupgrade image to the ''/tmp'' folder on the device. You will need to plug into **E1-E3** ports of the access point to reach OpenWrt, as E0 is the WAN port of the device. - Flash OpenWrt:\\ $ ubidetach -p /dev/mtd16 $ ubiformat /dev/mtd16 $ sysupgrade -n /tmp/openwrt-sysupgrade.bin
openwrt_wiki.back_to_stock:
To go back to the stock firmware, simply reset the bootcmd in the
bootloader to the original value:

  $ setenv bootcmd "boot"
  $ saveenv
  $ boot
  
If you are getting  <color #ed1c24>ls: ubi?: No such file or directory[   20.509806] UBIFS error (pid 1143): ubifs_mount: cannot open "/dev/ubifs", error -22
Get the stock firmware from https://networkingsupport.hpe.com/globalsearch#q=8.7.1.6&tab=Software&firstResult=10 and place if TFTP root

  $ upgrade os 1 192.168.1.75:ArubaInstant_Ursa_8.7.1.6_81786
  $ setenv bootcmd "boot"
  $ saveenv
  $ boot

if getting below error,
UBIFS error
cannot open "/dev/ubifs"
Mounting ubifs failed

  $ factory_reset
  $ boot
  
Factory credential is admin/SERIALNUMBEROFAP
openwrt_wiki.lan_switch:
The device has four switch ports. E0/PT you can use on the back of the device or below of the device

^ Port             ^ Switch Port   ^
| E0/PT (PoE-in)    | lan0          |
| E1                | lan1          |
| E2                | lan2          |
| E3    (PoE-out)   | lan3          |

Note that for bridged AP configuration use 'wan' not 'lan0'

  $ uci add_list network.@device[0].ports='wan'
openwrt_wiki.poe_passthrough: The magic numbers changed during the 6.1 -> 6.6 kernel update. === OpenWrt 24.10 === We need to deactivate GPIO **546** (low) for PoE Passthrough. echo "546" > /sys/class/gpio/export echo "out" > /sys/class/gpio/gpio546/direction echo "0" > /sys/class/gpio/gpio546/value We can configure this permanently in /etc/config/system (activating at boot): config gpio_switch 'poe_passthrough' option name 'PoE Passthrough' option gpio_pin '546' option value '0' === OpenWrt 23.05 and earlier === We need to deactivate GPIO 446 (low) for PoE Passthrough. echo "446" > /sys/class/gpio/export echo "out" > /sys/class/gpio/gpio446/direction echo "0" > /sys/class/gpio/gpio446/value We can configure this permanently in /etc/config/system (activating at boot): config gpio_switch 'poe_passthrough' option name 'PoE Passthrough' option gpio_pin '446' option value '0'
openwrt_wiki.gehaeuse_oeffnen:
To open the case, peel off the 4 white rubber feet and remove the torx T8 screws. There are no clips and the case separates easily.

When reassembling, be careful not to pinch the two antenna wires.

openwrt_commit.nachricht:
ipq40xx: add support for Aruba AP-303H

The Aruba AP-303H is the hospitality version of the Aruba AP-303 with a
POE-passthrough enabled ethernet switch instead of a sigle PHY.

Hardware
--------

SoC:   Qualcomm IPQ4029
RAM:   512M DDR3
FLASH: - 128MB SPI-NAND (Macronix)
       - 4MB SPI-NOR (Macronix MX25R3235F)
TPM:   Atmel AT97SC3203
BLE:   Texas Instruments CC2540T
       attached to ttyMSM1
ETH:   Qualcomm QCA8075
LED:   WiFi (amber / green)
       System (red / green /amber)
       PSE (green)
BTN:   Reset
USB:   USB 2.0

To connect to the serial console, you can solder to the labled pads next
to the USB port or use your Aruba supplied UARt adapter.

Do NOT plug a standard USB cable into the Console labled USB-port!
Aruba/HPE simply put UART on the micro-USB pins. You can solder yourself
an adapter cable:

VCC - NC
 D+ - TX
 D- - RX
GND - GND

The console setting in bootloader and OS is 9600 8N1. Voltage level is
3.3V.

To enable a full list of commands in the U-Boot "help" command, execute
the literal "diag" command.

Installation
------------

1. Get the OpenWrt initramfs image. Rename it to ipq40xx.ari and put it
   into the TFTP server root directory. Configure the TFTP server to
   be reachable at 192.168.1.75/24. Connect the machine running the TFTP
   server to the E0 (!) ethernet port of the access point, as it only
   tries to pull from the WAN port.

2. Connect to the serial console. Interrupt autobooting by pressing
   Enter when prompted.

3. Configure the bootargs and bootcmd for OpenWrt.
   $ setenv bootargs_openwrt "setenv bootargs console=ttyMSM0,9600n8"
   $ setenv nandboot_openwrt "run bootargs_openwrt; ubi part aos1;
     ubi read 0x85000000 kernel; set fdt_high 0x87000000;
     bootm 0x85000000"
   $ setenv ramboot_openwrt "run bootargs_openwrt;
     setenv ipaddr 192.168.1.105; setenv serverip 192.168.1.75;
     netget; set fdt_high 0x87000000; bootm"
   $ setenv bootcmd "run nandboot_openwrt"
   $ saveenv

4. Load OpenWrt into RAM:
   $ run ramboot_openwrt

5. After OpenWrt booted, transfer the OpenWrt sysupgrade image to the
   /tmp folder on the device. You will need to plug into E1-E3 ports of
   the access point to reach OpenWrt, as E0 is the WAN port of the
   device.

6. Flash OpenWrt:
   $ ubidetach -p /dev/mtd16
   $ ubiformat /dev/mtd16
   $ sysupgrade -n /tmp/openwrt-sysupgrade.bin

To go back to the stock firmware, simply reset the bootcmd in the
bootloader to the original value:

  $ setenv bootcmd "boot"
  $ saveenv

Signed-off-by: David Bauer <mail@david-bauer.net>

nachrichten.026fbd65:
026fbd650a58c22512ca64e85ccb5b318af3aaa7
ipq40xx: fix USB on Aruba AP-303H

Enable USB 3.0 controller, disable USB 2.0 controller.

The USB 2.0 port on the AP-303H is actually connected to the USB 3.0
controller's HS phy. Enable the HS phy only, since the SS lanes are not
brought out to the connector.

Signed-off-by: Ryan Salsbury <ryanrs@gmail.com>

ipq40xx: add PoE passthrough GPIO

Add the GPIO pin of the PoE passthrough switch on the Aruba AP-303H.
Power is activated when the pin is low. It enables a PSE chip, so power
is only supplied to downstream devices when they are 802.3af/at
compliant devices.

Ensure you use a sufficient power supply when chaining a consuming
device after the AP.

ipq40xx: fix I2C pin config on Aruba AP-303H

Turn on SoC pull-ups on I2C pins, since there are no discrete pull-up
resistors on the bus.

Increase clock to 400 kHz. Both chips on the bus support 400 kHz. I
tested the ISL28022 at 4,000 reads/sec and didn't see any garbled output
or bus hangs, even with SoC drive strength reduced to 2 for the test.

offene_faeden.grund: Block Diagram, Schematics, BOM, Operational Description nur 'Metadata only' (vertraulich)
User Manual 2 of 2 (3.8 MB, vermutlich Regulatory-Sammeldokument) und die älteren Fassungen vom 2017-07-08 nicht gelesen
Testberichte (Conducted 2.9 MB, DFS 2.9 MB, BLE 1.6 MB u. a.) und Test-Setup-Fotos nicht ausgewertet; Abweichung 2.4-GHz-Leistung Grant 17.6 dBm vs. MPE-Report 15.1 dBm offen
Wiki-Fotos aruba_303h_serial_console.jpg / _zoom.png und Konsolenkabel-Fotos nicht angesehen: Lage und Belegung der Lötpunkte neben dem USB-Port
aktuelle HPE-Fassung a00059878ENW nicht direkt geladen (nur Wayback-Snapshot vom 2024-10-03 der Fassung 2024-04-02); ältere Wayback-Fassungen ab 2017 nicht verglichen
Forumsthreads (u. a. Quelle des Wiki-Konsolenfotos, AP11D) nicht gelesen
Instant On AP11D: eigene FCC ID und Datenblatt nicht gesucht; Unterschiede zum AP-303H (Ports, PoE-Out, USB, Netzteil) offen
PoE-Out-Leistung im Handbuch widersprüchlich (13 W und 15 W), Datenblatt nennt nur 802.3af
Daten des Aruba-Netzteils AP-AC-48V36C (Strom, Stecker) nicht in den Quellen
Platinenaufdrucke (BY100B-1 ...) unscharf; ob es Hardware-Revisionen gibt, nennt keine Quelle

lauf.notiz: ToH-Dump eindeutig (pid 15680478). Datenseite, Wiki-Seite, Support-Commit, 6 Folge-Commits, DTS und generic.mk gelesen. FCC Q9DAPINH303: Installationshandbuch, Label, MPE-Report, Außen- und Innenfotos ausgewertet. Datenblatt a00059878ENW (2024) über Wayback (Original 403). DeviWiki und WikiDevi ohne Geräteseite. Werkstatt: AP11D = AP-303H-Hardware, AP-303-Bootloader nicht schreiben. Widersprüche: SPI-NOR MX25R3235F (Commit) vs MX25L3205D (Bootlog), PoE-Out 13 W vs 15 W (Handbuch), Ports im Wiki ('E0/PT') vs Datenblatt (E0 hinten, PT passiver Durchgang), Treiber ath10k vs ath10k-ct, 2.4-GHz-Leistung Grant vs MPE-Report.
